[DAY1 11:40:00 - DAY1 11:40:30]
I turn my head right, then back left. Lucia: "It was really popular some time ago." Katrina: "You can put it..." I nod and lean back. Lucia: "Yes, you can put it at the door. And the good thing about the cardboard dog is... If you want to make it simple, just cut the cardboard simply, then draw a dog head and stick it on. If you want it more complex, you need to cut more pieces and make a bigger one. I saw someone make a Doberman before; I haven't made that one myself — I just watched the tutorial; it seemed pretty easy. Just draw on the cardboard and cut it out easily." I glance right, then left while rocking my body back and forth and nodding slightly. I rest my hands on the stool and sit watching everyone, tilting my head right and nodding as I look at the whiteboard. Shure: "What we have plenty of is cardboard." Shure: "So I think this..."

[DAY6 16:42:00 - DAY6 16:45:00]
I begin working at the computer, pressing keys and monitoring its automatic responses while Shure debugs the system and searches for relevant videos. During this, Tasha and Nicous comment on the theme, discussing sapiosexuality and education levels, which prompts me to stand and move toward the living room door to investigate further.

Upon entering the living room upstairs, I observe the setup and listen to Lucia and Shure discussing a craft item—a small cardboard dog used as a substitute for a jellyfish lamp lacking a light bulb and stable legs. Lucia explains the eco-friendly nature of the item, made from delivery boxes, and prepares it for auction, while Shure sets up the presentation and engages the group with a microphone.

As the auction begins, I position myself in the living room corner with Violet and Nicous nearby, watching Shure introduce the first item and announce bids. A boy named Huang places bids starting at one coin, increasing to two coins, leading to the sale of Lucia’s toy dog. Following the transaction, I instruct Nicous to remember the details, and Tasha confirms the gift exchange, completing the auction segment before I turn left to proceed further.

[DAY4 15:30:00 - DAY4 15:33:00]
I enter the kitchen holding a durian, take several bites while adjusting my glasses, and check my reflection in the mirror. Then I visit Shure's room, where Xiu Shuo and Nicous are sitting on the bed, take another bite of durian, and return to the living room. After briefly checking the weather by opening the door, I continue eating durian as I move between rooms, occasionally interacting with others such as Alice on her phone and Lucy drinking water, demonstrating a casual observation of my surroundings before initiating work.

I gather everyone in the living room and announce the start of work, sitting on the bench near the entrance to assign tasks and discuss unboxing recent deliveries. I suggest tidying up the second floor as part of the organization process and inquire about the team's plans regarding "making dogs" or "looking at dogs." I propose first establishing some logic by observing the dogs before creating representations based on them, emphasizing that this logic is primarily for people. This sets a structured approach for the creative task ahead.

During the discussion, I observe Shure pacing while Katrina explains the styles of dogs to the group. Nicous asks for clarification about the meaning of "making dogs," and I explain that the process involves transforming cardboard into dog shapes by drawing rough outlines without worrying too much about details like the head. Lucia confirms this approach, and the team exchanges comments on related topics such as game mechanics and AI behavior. The conversation includes casual remarks and laughter as I eat durian, maintaining a collaborative atmosphere.

Lucy then approaches me in front of the whiteboard, requesting a pen suitable for drawing lines on cardboard. I inquire about the availability of colored pens previously purchased, and Lucia informs me that the team has gone paperless and currently lacks pens. I confirm that the pens have not yet arrived, highlighting a logistical issue that could impact the creative process. Meanwhile, Shure suggests imagining a paper dog as an alternative, indicating the team’s willingness to adapt to the current constraints.

[DAY1 11:39:00 - DAY1 11:49:00]
**Lucia proposes Earth Day DIYs (jellyfish lamps, cardboard dog, short skit)** Lucia presented three DIY ideas—jellyfish lamps using bubble tea cup lids and kits, cardboard dogs of varying complexity, and a short skit—emphasizing eco-friendliness and materials (kits, hot glue gun, cardboard). I listened attentively (moved, sat, lay face-down briefly, nodded, leaned forward/back, walked to the kitchen and back), verbally affirmed (“Yeah,” “Bought it”), and suggested using ready-made scripts if time is short; Shure confirmed cardboard availability. Conclusion: the group accepted these as feasible Earth Day options, with the skit flagged as harder to implement.

**Whiteboard/name clarification and brief banter** The team reviewed names on the whiteboard and corrected a backward name and strokes; Alice, Katrina, Shure, and I discussed symmetry and joked about mutations. I inspected the board closely, commented, laughed, and nodded while the group resolved the writing. Conclusion: the whiteboard was adjusted and group moved on.

**Tasha demonstrates seed paper and petri-dish hydroponics** Tasha showed seed paper made from discarded coffee grounds containing sunflower seeds that can sprout (petri-dish hydroponics can show sprouting in ~5 days); she displayed multiple designs. I retrieved and handed papers, opened boxes, checked the petri-dish delivery status on my phone/WeChat (scrolled, typed, then set phone down), watched Tasha’s demonstration, and repeatedly nodded. Conclusion: seed paper and petri-dish sprouting were accepted as eco-friendly activity options.

**Alice proposes wildlife puzzle and daffodil-bulb prizes** Alice proposed a challenging wildlife puzzle representing Earth harmony and suggested giving narcissus (daffodil) bulbs as participant prizes, offering to purchase quality bulbs. I observed, nodded, laughed, applauded, and acknowledged the prize idea. Conclusion: puzzle plus bulb prizes were added to the activity list.

**Katrina’s planting kits and Shure’s auction/cardboard idea** Katrina mentioned Haidilao’s strawberry planting kit and other planting options; group noted planting kits and short-term sprouting. Shure proposed a second-hand auction and reiterated cardboard availability. I reacted verbally (“Haidilao,” “Let’s go plant trees by the sea”), shifted positions, clapped, and rose as Shure began detailing his auction idea. Conclusion: the team accumulated four activities and progressed to Shure’s pitch.

[DAY4 16:27:00 - DAY4 17:27:00]
I interacted closely with a playful puppy in the yard, observing and engaging in its behaviors such as shaking, rolling on the grass, and playful biting. I patted its head, asked it to shake hands, and occasionally picked it up while managing its biting attempts to maintain safety. Others present, including Alice, Nicous, Lucia, and the Puppy Boss, shared detailed information about the puppy’s habits, health status, and vaccinations, which I confirmed directly with the owner. We discussed the puppy’s breed, the use of clothing, and teething behavior, while I took photos and helped enforce safety rules, notably preventing the puppy from biting electrical cords. The group recounted anecdotes about the puppy’s past behavior, and I balanced direct interaction, observation, and group conversation before concluding the visit with the puppy to ensure a comprehensive understanding and safe environment.

While seated, I prepared electronic equipment essential for our research by setting up a data cable connected to augmented glasses and a power bank. I explained to the group the nature of our research project: recreating a house environment equipped with multiple cameras and an experimental technology called "Facebook mate," developed as part of a school project at Nanyang Technological University, Singapore. I emphasized that the product was in an experimental and costly stage, highlighting strict usage rules including everyone inserting a research-related tube and preventing the puppy from biting cords. During this setup, I multitasked by monitoring the yard and maintained communication with the puppy’s owner and others, ensuring smooth coordination between equipment preparation and animal safety.

In conversations with Nicous and other guests, I gathered background information about a dorm mate’s academic journey, which spanned several universities. We engaged in detailed discussions about cat and dog breeds, their behavioral traits, and territorial instincts, particularly focusing on the puppy’s teething habits and biting tendencies. I provided guidance during guest interactions, cautioning them on safety measures around the puppy to avoid injury or damage. The dialogue extended into light social exchanges where I shared jokes about AI testing and discussed previous related projects, including collaboration with Tokyo University. These discussions clarified our experimental approach and reinforced the importance of maintaining hypotheses without adjustment, framing our research as primarily observational and methodologically rigorous.

After completing outdoor activities, I coordinated the group’s movement by directing everyone upstairs and through gate exits, suggesting a casual wandering since there was no specific destination planned. During our neighborhood walk, we corrected an initial wrong turn and decided to take a loop to enjoy the breeze. I pointed out local landmarks and initiated conversations about technology, including Xiaomi cars. We reviewed the day’s task progress, confirming that most objectives had been met and discussed the remaining tasks ahead. The group then shifted focus to deciding on food choices and noted cultural observations such as the temporary "Fu" character displayed on the ground, marking a transition from work-related activities to social and cultural engagement.

Upon entering a home yard, I engaged with Shure and Katrina regarding an activity involving flower pressing and examined various props for potential use in the project. Moving indoors to the kitchen, I discussed culinary preparations with Tasha and Lucia, focusing on roasting sweet potatoes without charcoal. Together, we devised a simplified cooking method suitable for the environment. Concurrently, I adjusted furniture and organized clothes hangers on a drying rack outside. I monitored the power status of our devices with Shure and detected issues despite confirmed power connections. I then used my phone to troubleshoot these technical problems, aiming to resolve them promptly while coordinating activities with everyone present to maintain workflow continuity.

Beginning with checking my phone, I engaged in conversations with Shure and Nicous regarding a phone issue and a missing or uncharged device. I greeted Katrina at the house entrance before entering the living room, where I interacted with the group. I instructed Alice to locate her charging cable and teased Tasha about her device’s battery status. Subsequently, I moved to the bedroom containing multiple computers, signaling a shift in tasks and location as I focused on resolving device-related issues and equipment management within this area.

In the bedroom, I handled a power bank and data cables, handing the power bank to Tasha who connected it to my glasses. I placed a data cable on a table outside where friends were gathered, then returned indoors to continue searching for a missing item. After failing to locate it in the bedroom, I directed Tasha to check the kitchen, where she found the item. I carried the power bank back outside and instructed the group to plug it in and power it on. Then I moved back inside and proceeded upstairs, passing through various rooms, thereby managing equipment deployment and ensuring power connectivity across locations.

Outside, I observed Shure tuning his guitar while Katrina and Nicous engaged nearby. I inquired about an item related to bees and suggested ordering takeout or cooking as meal options. I announced it was time to perform musically and clarified who would sing, noting some confusion with names. Shure explained his use of an AI app for guitar tuning and described previous methods based on vibration and feel. Nicous assisted in the tuning process while I managed the technical discussion leading up to the musical session, coordinating roles and ensuring readiness for recording.

During the music session, I coordinated filming efforts, encouraged group participation, and monitored progress closely. Technical issues arose with my phone’s timer and alarm, which I managed by resetting them and pausing filming with “Stop, cut,” then resuming after confirming everyone was ready. I oversaw the setup alongside Lucia and Alice’s activities and eventually moved upstairs to transition to a new task, maintaining oversight of both technical and social aspects during the session.

Upstairs, I inspected equipment and cameras, powered down my phone after reviewing chat history, and then descended to engage with Alice and Lucia. We shared a brief playful moment before focusing on installing a mechanical part. I examined and attempted to fit the piece, receiving guidance from Lucia to avoid forcing it and acknowledging possible future disassembly if necessary. We continued assembly by connecting a strip to the frame and adjusting components, with Lucia instructing and reassuring me through difficulties, ensuring proper installation and avoiding damage.

I assisted in pressing and fitting panels using mortise and tenon joint techniques, resolving fitting issues pointed out by Alice. We secured a plastic panel tightly to ensure stability. I tightened a ring and adjusted middle and bottom components with Lucia’s guidance, organized my belongings, and managed minor mishaps such as dropping the power bank. Tasha joined us with suggestions for evening plans. We completed the box setup with final board alignments and minor corrections, concluding the installation satisfactorily despite small imperfections, marking a key milestone in the assembly process.

Following Lucia’s instructions, I fastened a brittle plastic piece securely using clips, confirming completion of the debugging process. Along with Lucia and Shure, I addressed a noisy mechanism by adjusting alignment and tightening parts, achieving adequate stability. We prepared for the next activity by laying a new tablecloth and discussing missing parts, while identifying a headphone cover, thereby organizing our workspace and ensuring readiness for upcoming tasks.

Outside, I joined the group singing and observing guitar playing, noting Shure’s comments about teaching Xie Bin guitar. I requested Shure to play a song, watched Nicous read lyrics and play guitar, and shared the moment with others including Tasha and Katrina. I entered rooms observing interactions between Nicous and Shure, noted Lucia repairing components, and monitored the environment as I moved through the house. I engaged with people and oversaw ongoing tasks such as Lucia’s drawer assembly, maintaining active involvement throughout the diverse activities and ensuring smooth coordination among participants.

[DAY4 16:29:00 - DAY4 16:29:29]
I touch my arm and talk to the puppy's owner, petting the puppy as it lies down while I introduce the research project. "It's not mass-produced," I say. "You can't buy it yet," I add. Lucia: "It's in the experimental stage." "Right," I say. "Uh, it's part of the school's research — school, yeah," I say. "And this product is... What's it called? Facebook, Facebook, Facebook mate. Just... it's like $8000," I say.
